thread:
alex: Heads up — major customer (DataStream) escalated: tool calls that include binary payloads are intermittently failing and generating "error: malformed tool args". Repro on py + go SDKs.

support-bot: Created INC-8921 for DataStream. Priority: P1. Linked customer thread: https://support.example.com/tickets/8921 :rotating_light:

alex: Quick repro I ran locally (py):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
cli = RedwoodClient(api_key=.. )
resp = cli.call_tool("ocr_extract", file_bytes=b"\x00%PDF-1.4...")
print(resp)
# -> {"error": "malformed tool args: schema mismatch"}
```

jamie: Can you paste the raw request body that hits our gateway? Need to see the base64 payload. Also which SDK versions?

alex: py-sdk 0.11.7, go-sdk 0.9.3, ts-sdk 1.4.2. Raw body (gateway capture):
```json
{"tool":"ocr_extract","args":{"file_bytes":"AAJVUERGLTEuNA==","metadata":{}}}
```
(note: base64 decodes to leading 0x00 + "%PDF-1.4")

maria: Interesting — our tool selector lambda uses a schema-based discriminator that expects the bytes field to be a bare base64 string without leading NULs in some clients. I'm seeing TS client calls where the base64 begins with "JVBER" (no leading AA) while py shows "AAJVBER".

sam: SDK team triage: filing notes — this smells like inconsistent framing between SDK serializers. Go SDK uses a protobuf wrapper that encodes a 1-byte length/marker when the first byte is 0x00 (legacy behavior), py-sdk encodes the raw bytes which then get base64-encoded and include the 0x00. Gateway validation expects a specific schema (bytes -> base64 raw), so the extra marker triggers schema validation failure and fallback to error path.

alex: Because of the validation failure the request falls into our billing fallback path and logs as malformed args which also spikes error rates on the customer account. Customer is seeing token usage/billing anomalies.

maria: Quick mitigation — we can add a lax-bytes compatibility rule in the selector: accept leading 0x00 and strip before schema check. Patch ready for canary.

sam: Parallel SDK fix: pushing go-sdk 0.9.4 that removes the legacy length marker and aligns framing with py/ts. Also cut py-sdk 0.11.8 that normalizes bytes encoding when sending tool args. Workaround for customers in the meantime: preprocess file_bytes with `file_bytes = file_bytes.lstrip(b"\x00")` or set header `X-Redwood-Bytes-Mode: raw`.

jamie: Can you include a minimal curl for support to repro and attach logs to the ticket? I'll loop SOC.

alex: Curl I used: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"tool":"ocr_extract","args":{"file_bytes":"AAJVUERGLTEuNA=="}}'
```

ops-bot: Deploy canary patch to us-west-2 at 2024-12-09T14:22:00Z (rollout id: deploy-cc-1148).

maria: Canary up — added compatibility check + strip rule for leading null byte on tool args. Early telemetry: error rate for DataStream dropped from 6.2% -> 0.4% in canary region.

sam: SDKs published: go-sdk 0.9.4, py-sdk 0.11.8, ts-sdk 1.4.3. Release notes: "Normalize bytes framing for tool args to avoid leading marker; add opt-in compatibility header". Please advise customers to upgrade.

alex: I notified the customer, they confirmed canary fixed their repro. Keeping ticket open until global rollout. Thanks all. :tada:
